title: Cohort Retention Analysis Pipeline
description:
A `user_activity` table logs user engagement by date (with associated revenue). Build a **cohort retention report**: assign each user to a monthly cohort based on their first activity date, then for each cohort show how many users were active in each subsequent month (period 0 = acquisition month).

**Table: user_activity**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| user_id | INT |
| activity_date | DATE |
| revenue | NUMERIC(10,2) |

Output columns: `cohort_month`, `period` (months since first activity), `cohort_size`, `active_users`, `retention_pct` (rounded to 1 decimal). Order by `cohort_month`, `period`.
solution_sql: WITH cohort_base AS (SELECT user_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', MIN(activity_date))::DATE AS cohort_month FROM user_activity GROUP BY user_id), user_months AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', activity_date)::DATE AS active_month FROM user_activity), cohort_sizes AS (SELECT cohort_month, COUNT(*) AS cohort_size FROM cohort_base GROUP BY cohort_month), retention_data AS (SELECT cb.cohort_month, um.active_month, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM AGE(um.active_month, cb.cohort_month))::INT AS months_since_start, COUNT(DISTINCT um.user_id) AS active_users FROM cohort_base cb JOIN user_months um ON cb.user_id = um.user_id GROUP BY cb.cohort_month, um.active_month) SELECT r.cohort_month, r.months_since_start AS period, cs.cohort_size, r.active_users, ROUND(100.0 * r.active_users / cs.cohort_size, 1) AS retention_pct FROM retention_data r JOIN cohort_sizes cs ON r.cohort_month = cs.cohort_month ORDER BY r.cohort_month, r.months_since_start

test_cases.description: Cohort retention for January, February, and March cohorts

hints: Build the pipeline in four CTEs: (1) cohort_base assigns each user their cohort month via DATE_TRUNC on their MIN(activity_date); (2) user_months finds all distinct months each user was active; (3) cohort_sizes counts users per cohort; (4) retention_data joins cohort_base with user_months and uses EXTRACT(MONTH FROM AGE(...)) to compute months since acquisition.

EXTRACT(MONTH FROM AGE(active_month, cohort_month)) gives the integer number of months between two month-truncated dates within the same year. Final SELECT joins retention_data with cohort_sizes to compute retention_pct = active_users / cohort_size × 100.
explanation: This query chains four CTEs to build a complete cohort retention analysis. First, each user's cohort is their first-ever active month (DATE_TRUNC + MIN). Second, all months each user appeared are collected. Third, the cohort size is computed once per cohort. Fourth, these are joined to compute how many cohort members were active in each subsequent month, with AGE() measuring the elapsed months. The final SELECT computes retention percentage. All three cohorts have 100% retention at period 0 (acquisition month), then decay over time — user 3 from the January cohort is the only one still active at period 3. This is the foundation of subscription health dashboards at every SaaS company.
